svg.text: Decision guide — which lane, at which moment
Has the committee been granted an exemption
from OSD for this project?
yes (Metanorma/Git lane)
Git-native lane (this document)
commenter + GitHub issues + Metanorma CI;
disposition sheets generated; STS XML to ISO CS.
no (default)
Whole project in OSD (drafting, comments,
ballots) — and the team needs no Git history?
yes
OSD-native lane
authoring, commenting, and ballots entirely
in OSD; exports taken when needed.
partly / needs both
Which part runs
where?
Hybrid (bridged) — diagram 03
drafting + ledger in Git; the formal ballot
imported into OSD (I1–I4); results exported
back (E1–E3).
Any lane may fall back mid-flight (F1–F4, diagram 04):
• OSD unavailable → freeze STS snapshot (F1), continue in Git (F2), ballots via ISO CS (F3),
re-sync on recovery (F4). The Directives bind the artifacts and decisions, not the tooling.
• An exemption can be requested when the project enters the committee work programme.
When OSD gains STS round-trip and comment upload:
• EXTRACT E1–E3 collapse to one export+import step; IMPORT I2–I3 collapse to an STS push.
• The Git ledger remains the disposition history; OSD becomes the ballot surface.
• Revisit this guide per ballot — the lanes are converging, the Directives obligations are not changing.
Decision inputs: committee position on OSD (default/exemption), need for Git history and CI-rendered artifacts, stage timing
(a stage about to ballot argues for OSD; a stage in heavy drafting argues for the Git lane), and the secretariat's distribution
requirements (disposition DOCX + fixed document + STS XML — both lanes produce all three).
